questions.prompt: Find \(\dim(P_3)\), where \(P_3\) is the space of polynomials of degree at most 3.
questions.answer: A standard basis for \(P_3\) is \(\{1,x,x^2,x^3\}\). This basis has four vectors. Therefore \(\dim(P_3)\) = 4.
A \(2\times 2\) matrix has four independent entries: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right. A standard basis has four matrices E11, E12, E21, and E22. Therefore \(\dim(V)\) = 4.

questions.prompt: Find the dimension of the subspace of \(P_3\) consisting of polynomials p with \(p(0)\) = 0.
questions.answer: A polynomial in \(P_3\) has form \(a+bx+cx^2+dx^3\). The condition \(p(0)=0\) gives \(a=0\). Therefore \(p(x)=bx+cx^2+dx^3\). A basis is \(\{x,x^2,x^3\}\), which has three vectors. Hence the dimension is 3.

questions.prompt: Find the dimension of the vector space of \(2\times 3\) real matrices.
questions.answer: A \(2\times 3\) matrix has \(2\cdot3\) = 6 independent entries. A standard basis contains one matrix for each entry position. Therefore the dimension of \(M_{2,3}(\mathbb R)\) is 6.

questions.prompt: Find the dimension of the subspace of \(2\times 2\) matrices with trace 0.
questions.answer: A general \(2\times 2\) matrix with trace 0 has form \(\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&-a\end{pmatrix}\), because the diagonal entries must sum to 0. This is a\(\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}\) + b\(\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}\) + c\(\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\). These three matrices are independent and span the subspace. Therefore the dimension is 3.

questions.prompt: Find the dimension of the subspace of \(P_2\) consisting of constant polynomials.
questions.answer: A constant polynomial has form \(p(x)=a\). The set is spanned by the single polynomial 1, because every constant polynomial is \(a\cdot1\). Since 1 is non-zero, {1} is a basis. Therefore the dimension is 1.

questions.prompt: A vector space has a basis with 6 vectors. What is its dimension?
questions.answer: The dimension of a vector space is the number of vectors in any basis. If a basis has 6 vectors, then the dimension is 6.

questions.prompt: Can \(P_2\) have a basis with four vectors? Explain.
questions.answer: No. \(P_2\) has standard basis \(\{1,x,x^2\}\), so \(\dim(P_2)\) = 3. All bases of a finite-dimensional vector space have the same number of vectors. Therefore every basis for \(P_2\) has exactly three vectors, not four.

questions.prompt: Find the dimension of the subspace of \(P_3\) spanned by {1 + x, x + \(x^2\), \(x^2\) + \(x^3\)}. Assume these three polynomials are independent, and explain the result.
questions.answer: If the three listed polynomials are independent, then they form a basis for their span. The dimension of a span is the number of vectors in a basis for that span. Since this independent spanning set has three vectors, the dimension is 3.

questions.prompt: A learner says \(\dim(V)\) = n because the highest power is x^n. Diagnose the error.
questions.answer: The space \(P_n\) contains polynomials of degree at most n, so a standard basis is {1, x, \(x^2\), ..., x^n}. This list has n + 1 vectors because it includes the constant term 1 = x^0. Therefore \(\dim(P_n)\) = n + 1, not n.
